paragraphs: I am Lily, and I live with Mom, Dad, Tom, and Pip. On Saturday evening, we have a problem. Dad wants to watch a concert on the TV. But the TV remote is not on the table. "I need to change the channel," says Dad. Mom is in the kitchen, and she makes a delicious dinner. The dinner smells very good. Tom and I must find the remote. The concert begins in ten minutes.

"What does it look like?" asks Tom. "Tell me, and I can look for it," he says. I think about the remote, and I describe it. Tom listens very carefully. "It is long and black," I say. "It is small, and it fits in my hand." "It has a big red button at the top." "The back is gray, and it has two small batteries."

Tom looks on the sofa and under the table. He looks behind the TV too. He looks in Mom's shopping bag and at the garden door. He looks in my school bag too. There is no remote. "Is it square?" he asks. "No, it is a long rectangle," I say. "It has round buttons, and a quiz channel button is blue." Dad likes quiz programs on that channel.

Then Pip barks near his basket. Tom looks into the small basket. Under Pip's blanket, there is something long and black. It is the remote! "Good dog, Pip!" says Tom. Dad laughs and turns on the concert. He says thank you to Pip. Mom calls us for dinner. Pip sits on the sofa, and he looks very happy.
